origin_excerpts.quote: - Facilitator note — freeze and refusal (read carefully): the Corrections scenario turns on a real distinction this lesson teaches behaviorally — in the scenario, silence under pressure is **not** the same act as a deliberate refusal to answer. Teach it at that level: as a distinction between two behaviors in a described situation, and as a reason to ask what happened before interpreting silence. Do **not** teach it as a diagnosis of any participant, do not label any participant's silence in the room as “freeze,” and do not use any clinical or nervous-system label for it — the lesson files use none, and this guide adds none. Phase 4 evidence review found general support for the concept that freezing can be involuntary; it did not establish a diagnostic test a facilitator can apply to a person in the room, and none is offered here.
